Replace the LightGBM regressor with catboost.CatBoostRegressor (500 iterations, same learning rate, verbose output off, seeded). The spec mentions RandomForestRegressor, but train.py already uses LightGBM, so this swaps LightGBM for CatBoost.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the Morgan radius from 2 to 3. It adds no file or network access, no hardcoded answers and no use of test labels.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The change is a single hyperparameter.

Recomputed z = (0.5954 - 0.6285) / (0.0042 * sqrt(2)) ≈ -5.57. The harness reports -5.580. The small gap is probably because the harness uses unrounded values. Either way the candidate is clearly worse by about 0.033 MAE, so 'reject' is correct.
Small caveat: the incumbent has only 1 run, but the gap is about 8 noise sd, so one run is enough here.

description: Change the Morgan fingerprint RADIUS constant from 2 to 3 so each count feature captures larger atom environments, keeping the LightGBM model and count featurization unchanged.
Abort the Increase Radius idea: changing RADIUS from 2 to 3 was already tested in slot 9 and rejected (0.6285, +0.0331 vs incumbent 0.5954).
Append three RDKit physchem descriptors (MolWt, TPSA, MolLogP) to the Morgan count fingerprint before fitting LightGBM. MaxAbsFreq is not a real RDKit descriptor, so it is left out.
Add min_child_samples=50 (the scikit-learn name for LightGBM's min_data_in_leaf) to the LGBMRegressor so that leaves must contain at least 50 molecules, to reduce overfitting.

Increase N_TREES from 500 to 1000 in the LightGBM regressor, keeping the learning rate at 0.05, to test whether more boosting rounds capture more interactions in the Morgan count plus physchem features.

Abort: the N_TREES increase repeats slot 12 (500 to 1000 LightGBM trees, 0.5466, delta -0.0033, rejected as within noise), and the spec's Random Forest and 300-tree baseline no longer exist in train.py.
Abort: the XGBoost gamma idea has no target, because train.py uses LGBMRegressor and XGBoost was already tested and rejected in slot 2.

CatBoost has no 'dart' boosting type (its boosting_type is only Ordered or Plain), so I applied the closest valid version: LightGBM's own DART boosting (boosting_type='dart') on the current LGBMRegressor, leaving everything else unchanged.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only changes two hyperparameters: N_TREES goes from 500 to 1000 and LEARNING_RATE from 0.05 to 0.02. It adds no file or network access, no hard-coded predictions and no use of test labels.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. N_TREES × LEARNING_RATE drops from 25 to 20, so total boosting shrinkage is a bit lower, but this is a normal tuning change.

Recomputed z = (0.5500 − 0.549) / (0.0042·√2) ≈ 0.168. This agrees with the harness value of 0.171, which probably used unrounded values. A gain of about 0.001 is well within noise, so 'reject' is the right decision.
Side note: doubling the number of trees roughly doubles the boosting cost. Check that the job still finishes well inside the 10-minute limit.

description: Lower LightGBM's learning rate from 0.05 to 0.02 and raise N_TREES from 500 to 1000, a slower-learning schedule that differs from the earlier tree-count-only test (slot 12).
Add lambda_l1=0.1 (L1 regularization on leaf values) to the LGBMRegressor parameters to test whether it helps with the 2048-bit count fingerprint space.

Abort: changing RADIUS from 2 to 3 was already tested (slot 9, official 0.6285 vs 0.5954 at the time, a +0.0331 regression well beyond the 0.0042 noise), and the current incumbent still uses radius 2, so this would repeat a rejected experiment.
Append 167-bit MACCS keys (via rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, since Chem.DataStruct.GetMACCSKeys does not exist in RDKit) to the Morgan count and RDKit descriptor features in featurize.

Abort the target mean centering idea: LightGBM's default boost_from_average already starts every model at the training mean, so subtracting and re-adding the mean would produce the same model and waste a slot.

Abort the seed-bagged LGBM ensemble: with the current deterministic LightGBM settings (no row or column subsampling), three seeds give identical models, so the change is a no-op that only triples runtime.

Lower LightGBM LEARNING_RATE from 0.05 to 0.01 and raise N_TREES from 500 to 2000 to test a finer learning-rate schedule; this is not a repeat of slot 14 (0.02 with 1000 trees), so it is worth one slot.

Abort: the idea targets a RandomForestRegressor with max_features='sqrt', but train.py has no random forest; it uses LGBMRegressor, and the closest equivalent (per-tree feature subsampling via colsample_bytree=0.3) was already tested in slot 3 and rejected (0.5924, delta -0.0030, within noise).

Abort: standardizing the fingerprint features before LightGBM would not change the model, because tree splits depend only on feature ordering and LightGBM bins each feature, so a per-feature scaler is a monotone transform with no effect.
Aborted the log1p target-transform idea: log1p is undefined for logD values at or below -1, which this data contains, and the target is not strongly skewed.
Standardize the concatenated Morgan-count, descriptor and MACCS features using training-set mean and standard deviation before LightGBM.

Abort the feature-scaling idea: StandardScaler on the count fingerprints is a per-feature monotonic transform, so LightGBM's histogram binning and split choices are unchanged and the job would just reproduce the incumbent at a cost of one slot.
Abort: LightGBM's default min_data_in_leaf is already 20, so setting min_data_in_leaf=20 is a no-op, and the only related change (min_child_samples=50, slot 11) was worse at 0.5610.
Abort: setting MAX_FEATURES to 0.1 for a RandomForestRegressor has no target, because train.py uses LGBMRegressor and MAX_FEATURES is never passed to it.
Abort the target mean-centering idea because LightGBM's default boost_from_average already starts the L2 model at the training mean, so the change would not alter the fit.
Aborted the Morgan FP Bit Count idea: the spec would switch the current count fingerprint back to binary bits, which slot 1 already showed is worse, so the slot is not worth spending.

Abort: the XGBoost swap (with depth 6, learning rate 0.05 and subsample 0.8) repeats slot 2, which replaced LightGBM with XGBoost and was rejected at 0.6395 (+0.0440 vs the incumbent), and the incumbent LightGBM model is still better.

Append heavy atom count, rotatable bonds and aromatic ring count to the RDKit descriptor block, using the real RDKit names (Descriptors.HeavyAtomCount, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings) because the spec's NumHeavyDosers and NumAromatic do not exist.

Abort: switching Morgan features back to 4096-bit vectors would undo the accepted count-fingerprint change (slot 1, which cut loss from 0.6663 to 0.5954), so it is unlikely to help and does not merit a slot.

Wire the currently unused MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF constant into the LightGBM model as min_child_samples and set it to 5, to test whether a smaller minimum leaf size helps relative to LightGBM's default of 20 (slot 11 tested 50, which was worse).

Abort the XGBoost early-stopping idea: it requires swapping the LightGBM model for XGBoost, which was already tested and rejected (slot 2, 0.6395 vs incumbent 0.5320), and a validation split would also cut the training data.
Abort: the proposed max_depth=15 change targets a RandomForestRegressor, which train.py no longer uses (it now fits LGBMRegressor), so there is no parameter to edit.
